prompt: A hand-painted map of a whole continent seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges. One single continent fills most of the sheet, north at the top, with a margin of sea on every side so that no coast is cut off: open sea along the whole east and south, a narrower cold grey sea off the north-west. The land is one broad mass, a little wider than it is tall, about four fifths of the sheet across, nowhere pinched narrow, with an irregular coast. Across the whole north of the land runs one high mountain range crowned with ice and snow, west to east, thickest and highest in the north-west. From the middle of that range a lower spur of bare hills comes a short way south, with one clear gap through it. South of the mountains, across the north-west and the north, lies a broad band of pale dry steppe and high plain. In the north-east are stony grey uplands. In the west, rolling hill country where steppe, hills and river plain meet. In the south-west, one great dark forest, with open green grassland along its eastern edge and hills behind it. The center of the land is open rolling plain, and in the exact middle of the sheet stands one lone mass of low brown hills whose outline, seen from above, is plainly a huge four-legged beast lying curled asleep, head tucked to its flank: land in the shape of an animal, about a tenth of the sheet long, drawn as hills and nothing else. In the south, a wide flood plain of dark black-brown soil, with a line of low hills between it and the center. On the east coast, a little north of the middle, one broad bay with a small sheltered inlet in it. On the south-east coast, a great river delta with reed marsh round it. Rivers, each a fine dark line running downhill to a coast: one from the ice of the north-west mountains west across the steppe to the cold sea; one long river from the northern mountains south through the gap in the spur, braided in many channels across the northern plain, then south-east across the open center, passing east of the beast-shaped hills, to the delta; one from the stony north-east uplands south through braided reaches and reed country to the same delta; one wide slow river from the hills north of the dark plain south across it to the middle of the south coast; one from the western hills south-west through the grassland along the forest's edge to the south-west coast, with a short tributary out of the western hill country.
